title: Sweet & Sour Turkey Burgers
ingredients: ¼ cup red onion, finely diced (⅛ of whole)
method: Add all turkey patty ingredients (except olive oil) to a large bowl and mix well.
Shape into patties — the base recipe makes 6, but Amy typically gets 9 smaller patties.
Pan-fry in olive oil until cooked through and golden brown on both sides.
notes: Take the extra time to dice the red onion and bird's eye chillies as fine as possible — it helps make the texture smoother. Amy's batch size varies between 6–9 patties; macros are based on 9. Per patty (9/batch): ~11g protein, ~0.5g fibre, ~90 calories.

title: Chicken Sausage & Herby Egg Muffins
ingredients: 12 chicken patties (~87g each, from 1kg chicken mince)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C. Whisk eggs, milk, dill, spring onions, lemon zest, and salt together.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper, pour egg mixture in. Bake 15 mins, then cover with foil for 5 more mins if needed until set.
Cool, then slice the egg sheet into 12 equal squares.
Stack each muffin: English muffin → egg square → chicken patty → cheese slice.
Wrap individually in parchment paper. Refrigerate or freeze.
Reheat from fridge: 10 mins at 180°C. From freezer: thaw first, then same.
notes: Renee recommends making double — freeze half, keep the rest in the fridge. Per muffin: ~446 cal, 38g protein, 39g carbs, 15g fat. The chicken patty recipe is linked separately on Renee's Instagram.

title: 5-Ingredient Maple Sage Chicken Sausage Patties
method: Mix the spices (sage, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper) together.
Add spice mix and maple syrup to the chicken mince. Combine well.
Divide into desired patty size — larger for breakfast sausage, smaller for sliders.
Cook in a hot pan for a few minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
notes: Renee created this for the many people who can't or don't eat eggs but still want a prep-ahead breakfast protein. The psyllium husk is optional but adds fibre. The chicken patties can be used in the Herby Egg Muffins recipe (freeze extras). Macros are per patty for an 8-patty batch.
